outcome: Bladder neck size at rest and during maximum Valsalva maneuver
Proportion of patients with POP-Q stage 0/I
cohort: Women who had a first delivery and were in weeks 36-41 of a subsequent pregnancy (n=304)
finding: Second birth delivery mode and birth interval were associated with changes in maternal pelvic floor measures, with cesarean section associated with a smaller hiatus area and circumference and a longer birth interval associated with a smaller hiatus area and larger bladder neck size.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with a smaller hiatus area and circumference compared to vaginal delivery.
